notes: All lessons, questions, solved examples and diagram specifications independently authored; no copied textbook figures or question banks.
NCBI Bookshelf NBK7908 retrieval failed through scraper; it is NOT claimed as a read source and is not used as evidence.

OpenStax11.2 topoIV table contains a single-strand wording inconsistent with type-II double-strand gate; specialist source R12A11 controls the authored explanation. Lagging-strand synthesis is explicitly five-prime to three-prime.
OpenStax11.6 wording can blur specialized transduction and lysogenic conversion; authored text explicitly separates bacterial-gene transfer from phenotype encoded by prophage genes.
R12A4 coverage is abstract only; conclusions confined to the abstract’s decatenation finding.
Bacterial mapping examples are hypothetical educational data, not recalled official examination questions. Co-transfer percentages are conditional and not converted to exact physical distances.
Exam questions are tagged by chapter for parent to redistribute into four balanced comprehensive examinations across all ten chapters.
No claim that official 1406 coefficients or subject list has been independently verified in this subtask.
Final source cross-check added dedicated SOS (R12A12) and BER (R12A13) reviews; named sections actually read. Numerical exercises varied between time, speed and fraction copied.
